content: {"rule": "K-C", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge text grades a link collision by whether Isaiah 7:14's sign-sense is left open, which is a verse-level underdetermination ruling of the kind K-C governs when a link is pressed by the pressing side's own chain.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] G answers the 'almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows, leaving the sign's sense open.", "rule_words": "When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.", "room": "Phrase 'never verse by verse': I weighed reading one, which bars an UNDERDETERMINED ruling based on Isaiah 7:14's open sense as verse-by-verse, against reading two, which would allow that as a permissible conclusion after chain-against-chain footing.", "why": "By making the link UNDERDETERMINED because the sign's sense remains open, the judge used a verse-level openness test instead of weighing the relevant chains against each other by footing."}
